'''Ronald Brown [[Learned Society of Wales|FLSW]]''' (born 4 January 1935 – 6 December 2024) was an English mathematician. He was a [[Professor]] in the School of Computer Science at [[Bangor University]].<ref>https://web.archive.org/web/20150907221637/http://pages.bangor.ac.uk/~mas010/ Page at Bangor University, UK</ref> He authored many books and more than 160 journal articles. Brown died on 6 December 2024, at the age of 89.<ref>{{Cite news |date=4 January 2025 |title=Ronald Brown obituary |url=https://ronald-brown-1935-2024.muchloved.com/ |access-date=4 January 2025}}</ref>

==Education and career==
Born on 4 January 1935 in London, Brown attended [[Oxford University]], obtaining a [[Bachelor of Arts|B.A.]] in 1956 and a [[D.Phil.]] in 1962.<ref name=bio>{{cite web | url = http://www.bangor.ac.uk/~mas010/biog-br.html | title = Ronald Brown: Biographical Sketch | work = Bangor University | accessdate= 2010-04-23}}</ref> Brown began his teaching career during his doctorate work, serving as an assistant lecturer at the [[University of Liverpool]] before assuming the position of Lecturer. In 1964, he took a position at the [[University of Hull]], serving first as a Senior Lecturer and then as a Reader before becoming a Professor of [[pure mathematics]] at Bangor University, then a part of the [[University of Wales]], in 1970.

Brown served as Professor of Pure Mathematics for 30 years; he also served during the 1983–84 term as a Professor for one month at [[Louis Pasteur University]] in [[Strasbourg]].<ref name=bio/> In 1999, Brown took a half-time research professorship until he became Professor Emeritus in 2001. He was elected as a Fellow of the [[Learned Society of Wales]] in 2016.

==Editing and writing==
Brown served as an [[editor]] or on the [[editorial board]] for a number of print and [[electronic journal]]s. He began in 1968 with the ''[[Chapman & Hall]] Mathematics Series'', contributing through 1986.<ref name=bio/> In 1975, he joined the editorial advisory board of the [[London Mathematical Society]], remaining through 1994. Two years later, he joined the editorial board of [[Springer Science+Business Media|Applied Categorical Structures]],<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.bangor.ac.uk/~mas010/publicfull.htm | title = ''Applied Categorical Structures'' | work = Springer Publishers, Berlin | date = 2010-12-08 | accessdate = 2010-12-11}}</ref> continuing through 2007. From 1995 and 1999, respectively, he has been active with the electronic journals ''[http://www.tac.mta.ca/tac/ Theory and Applications of Categories]''<ref>EDITORIAL BOARD of the International journal ''Theory and Applications of Categories'' http://www.tac.mta.ca/tac/geninfo.html#edlist</ref> and ''[[Homology, Homotopy and Applications]]'',<ref>EDITORIAL BOARD of the International journal ''Homology, Homotopy and Applications'' http://www.intlpress.com/HHA/editors.htm</ref> which he helped found. Since 2006, he has been involved with ''[[arXiv|Journal of Homotopy and Related Structures]]''.<ref>Listed in the Editors' List of the International ''Journal of Homotopy and Related Structures'' http://tcms.org.ge/Journals/JHRS/editors.htm</ref> His mathematical research interests ranged from [[algebraic topology]] and [[groupoid]]s, to [[homology theory]], [[category theory]], [[mathematical biology]], [[mathematical physics]] and [[higher-dimensional algebra]].<ref>Editor Ronald Brown's research interests: Category theory, higher-dimensional algebra, holonomy, groupoids and crossed objects in algebraic topology. http://emis.kaist.ac.kr/journals/JHRS/interests.htm</ref><ref>Cited in {{cite journal

Brown authored or edited a number of books and over 160 academic papers published in academic journals or collections. His first published paper was "Ten topologies for X × Y", which was published in the ''Quarterly Journal of Mathematics'' in 1963.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.bangor.ac.uk/~mas010/publicfull.htm | title = Ronald Brown Publications | work = Bangor University | date = 2008-04-19 | accessdate = 2010-04-23 |archiveurl = https://web.archive.org/web/20080424002106/http://www.bangor.ac.uk/~mas010/publicfull.htm |archivedate = 2008-04-24}}</ref> Since then, his publications have appeared in many journals, including but not limited to the ''[[Journal of Algebra]]'', ''[[Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society]]'', ''[[Mathematische Zeitschrift]]'', ''[[College Mathematics Journal]]'', and ''[[American Mathematical Monthly]]''. He was also known for several recent co-authored papers on [[Ontology|categorical ontology]].<ref>Cited in Online research in philosophy Entries: http://philpapers.org/</ref>

Among his several books and standard topology and algebraic topology textbooks are: ''Elements of Modern Topology'' (1968), ''Low-Dimensional Topology'' (1979, co-edited with T.L. Thickstun), ''Topology: a geometric account of general topology, homotopy types, and the fundamental groupoid'' (1998),<ref>Cited in [[Encyclopaedia of Mathematics]] – {{ISBN|1-4020-0609-8}}</ref><ref>Referenced in [https://encyclopediaofmath.org/wiki/Algebraic_homotopy ''Algebraic homotopy'']</ref> ''Topology and Groupoids'' (2006)<ref name="myyn.org">Cited in "Bibliography For Groupoids And Algebraic Topology" http://myyn.org/m/article/bibliography-for-groupoids-and-algebraic-topology/</ref> and ''Nonabelian Algebraic Topology: Filtered Spaces, Crossed Complexes, Cubical Homotopy Groupoids'' (EMS, 2010).<ref name="myyn.org"/><ref>http://sz0009.ev.mail.comcast.net/service/home/~/Tracts_vol15.pdf?auth=co&loc=en_US&id=128480&part=2 and www.ems-ph.org : ''EMS Tracts in Mathematics'', Vol. 15</ref><ref>http://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/viewdoc/summary?doi=10.1.1.150.6444 CiteSeerX accessed on 12/10/2010</ref><ref>{{nlab|id=Nonabelian+Algebraic+Topology|title=Review of "Nonabelian Algebraic Topology"}}</ref><ref>A Review of "Nonabelian Algebraic Topology" by Prof. J. Baez on June 6, 2009 http://golem.ph.utexas.edu/category/2009/06/nonabelian_algebraic_topology.html</ref><ref>Addebook • Apr 22nd, 2009 • Category: Mathematics :'' Nonabelian Algebraic Topology'' http://www.addebook.com/tech2/mathematics/nonabelian-algebraic-topology_4164.html
</ref><ref>Cited on p. xi as a basic reference in "Non-abelian Theories" http://myyn.org/m/article/non-abelian-theories/</ref><ref>[ALGTOP-L] available full draft of book on ''Nonabelian algebraic topology'' https://lists.lehigh.edu/pipermail/algtop-l/2009q2/000443.html</ref><ref>Cited in "Towards Higher Categories" By John C. Baez and [[J. Peter May]], Publisher: Springer Verlag, Published Date: 2009-10-01, {{ISBN|978-1-4419-1523-8}} http://www.isbnlib.com/author/John_C__Baez</ref><ref>Referenced in {{nlab|id=nonabelian+cohomology|title=nonabelian cohomology}}</ref>

His recent fundamental results that extend the classical [[Seifert-van Kampen theorem|Van Kampen theorem]] to higher homotopy in higher dimensions (HHSvKT) are of substantial interest for solving several problems in algebraic topology, both old and new.<ref>The higher Van Kampen Theorems and computation of the unstable homotopy groups of spheres and complex spaces https://mathoverflow.net/q/39818</ref> Moreover, developments in algebraic topology have often had wider implications, as for example in [[algebraic geometry]] and also in [[algebraic number theory]]. Such higher-dimensional (HHSvKT) theorems are about homotopy invariants of structured spaces, and especially those for filtered spaces or ''n''-cubes of spaces. An example is the fact that the relative [[Witold Hurewicz|Hurewicz]] theorem is a consequence of HHSvKT, and this then suggested a triadic [[Hurewicz theorem]].
